Subject: HyperEdge AI — post-call technical summary & next steps

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap (call notes -> technical assumptions -> immediate asks) so we have shared alignment ahead of the PoC planning call. If I missed anything, flag it and we’ll update.

Call highlights / agreed goals:
- Customer pain: unpredictable latency spikes for user-facing ranking and high per-token cost on current hosted endpoints.
- Primary goal: <200–250ms p95 for 512-token generative responses while keeping unit cost < $0.003/token for the majority of traffic.
- Secondary: preserve model quality for long-form completions (support for ~2k token contexts).

Technical summary (what Redwood proposes for PoC):
- Target SLOs: latency p95 < 250ms at 512 tokens; p99 < 450ms during peak; steady-state throughput target 160–200 req/s for the pilot workload (90% small responses).
- Model variants: latency-critical path -> 13B quantized (4-bit) optimized kernels; high-quality fallback/off-peak -> 70B float16 variant.
- Serving topology: dedicated US‑West GPU pool for primary traffic with regional failover to hosted pools; optional Private (VPC) deployment for data residency.
- Runtime optimizations: continuous batching (max window 20ms), prefix/KV caching to reduce re-tokenization on repeat prompts (we estimate 25–35% token savings), and quantized kernels to keep VRAM footprints low.
- Autoscaling & fallbacks: canary rollouts + automatic fallback to a lower-precision variant when GPU capacity constrained.

Assumptions / open questions we need confirmed by HyperEdge before PoC:
1) Typical request size distribution (tokens in/out). Please share a small sample histogram.
2) Acceptable retention window for logs & traces (default 90 days vs enterprise retention).
3) Whether user-specific personalization requires per-user KV cache (impacts memory).
4) Procurement/contracting lead and any required security docs (SOC2, data flow diagrams).

Attachments: latency_and_throughput_projection_v1.pdf (projection based on your sample profile), deployment_topology_sketch_v1.png (high-level).

Proposed next steps / mutual action plan (brief):
- HyperEdge to confirm request-size histogram + procurement contact by 2026-04-22 (Alex).
- Redwood to deliver a PoC design doc and cost outline by 2026-04-27 (Chloe + Karthik).
- Target PoC start: week of 2026-05-04 (2-week pilot).

If the above looks good I’ll schedule a 45-minute infra deep-dive with Grace (our runtime/ops lead) — she’ll run through topology options and the resource profile we’d provision for the PoC.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the clear write-up, Chloe — this matches our expectations so far. A few clarifying items from our infra side: 

1) Memory footprint per model: can you provide rough VRAM numbers for the 13B quantized + 70B float16 variants under Redwood's runtime (including KV cache overhead)? We need to confirm feasible instance types (we currently prefer A10G/80GB A100 family).
2) Does prefix/KV caching support tenant-scoped caches? We plan to keep some per-customer personalization in memory during active sessions.
3) Network egress & data residency: can logs/traces be stored in our VPC/hosted S3? Also want to know if regional routing to EU is automatic or requires a separate private deployment.

On procurement: looping in procurement to start the standard NDA / SOW timeline conversation. Procurement will need SOC2 Type II and a data flow diagram before we can sign an engagement letter.

Happy to join the infra deep-dive; Alex (infra) and our procurement lead are available Apr 22–23 afternoon Pacific.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | HyperEdge.ai

Alex — quick answers inline and some ballpark numbers to help your capacity planning. Happy to refine on the deep-dive.

1) VRAM estimates (approx, runtime-dependent):
   - 13B quantized (4-bit + fused kernels): ~14–20GB VRAM (active KV cache adds ~2–6GB per large concurrent session depending on personalization).
   - 70B float16: ~48–64GB VRAM (we typically run this on 80GB A100s with tensor-parallel split; effective per-request latency higher).

2) Tenant-scoped KV cache: yes — runtime supports per-tenant/per-session KV caching. We can size cache persistence by tenant to bound memory.

3) Logs & data residency: we support exporting logs/traces to customer-owned S3 in a VPC (we can push via VPC endpoint). Regional routing requires a dedicated private deployment if you need strict EU-only residency; hosted routing can be configured for regional preference but is not a replacement for private deployments for regulatory guarantees.

Notes on infra: for the PoC we recommend a small dedicated pool of 3x A10G (for the 13B path) + 1x 80GB A100 for validation of the 70B variant and fallback testing. Continuous batching + prefix caching should keep p95 in target range for your request mix.

Proposed times: Apr 22, 2:00pm PT or Apr 23, 3:30pm PT for the infra deep-dive (Grace will lead). Which works for you?

I’ll also prepare a short cost/throughput matrix (Karthik) and send before the call.

-Chloe
